1.0.14: Every call on match day shows what you gain, what it costs and the odds.
League news covers every match of the round.
A Tribunal verdict shows whether your challenge won, the ban before and after, and what it cost you.
Each player's sheet tells the story of his career.
1.0.15: Build your own game plan on the Coaching screen: pick one strength and one cost, and name it.
Full time tells you what each of your calls led to.
Every draftee shows a real AFL player he plays like.
Players can earn up to five traits.
The papers' pre-season ladder has a line on every club, and your practice match can move you a place or two.
Your press interview comes before the draft, in the press room.
1.0.16: Fixed: a sacked coach who takes a new job now runs his new club from the day he signs, not the club that sacked him.
Match day has a new look: weather, night games, tighter call scenes with both sides in place, and a bench drawer you tap open.
Team selection marks the players in the worst and best form, and players left out now play reserves games.
The training report has a Learn button for every player who can learn a position.
The hub tells you the week your fitness plan can change.
Fixed: the press no longer says the board hears excuses after a win.
1.0.17: Legacy: start a career in 1990, 2000, 2010 or 2020 with that year's real lists, coaches, captains, guernseys, grounds, fixtures and rules, or in 2028 with Tasmania or 2030 with Canberra.

Every season after your start rolls over as the real league did: Fitzroy's merger, the Bears or the Lions, new clubs coming in, the supplements saga (with its own switch), and Tasmania and Canberra joining.
Real careers go into the drafts, and money is counted in each season's dollars.
The weather can turn at a break, and the match plays on in the new conditions.
100 new achievements: a rivalry and a dynasty feat for every club, and 56 for the coach.
Team selection and the player sheet show fatigue, morale and form as numbers.
Coach of the Year is decided on the home-and-away season, before the finals, with why he won it.
Fixed: a draft-night pick trade shows before the pick it bought, not after.
Fixed: a coach who signs with a new club no longer runs the old club's off-season.
